learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge will be provided on the methods of schematization of simple mechanical systems and on those for evaluating the state of stress.
Knowledge will also be provided on the mechanical properties of materials and methods for sizing and verifying components subjected to static and fatigue loads.
Knowledge will also be provided on the main machine elements used in the design of mechanical systems and on design, selection and verification methodologies.
Students will be able to apply design elements to individual machine components.
Students will be able to understand and assemble components to obtain the design of machines and groups.
Students will be able to design, choose and verify the main machine elements used in the creation of simple mechanical systems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the concepts of probability and reliability
Materials: Generalities and recalls on characteristics and properties of metallic materials
Static load conditions: Resistance criteria for yielding and fracture of ductile and brittle materials
Fatigue load conditions: Fatigue behavior of materials (S-N)
Factors influencing the fatigue strength of components and machines
Structural connections: Principles of force transfer
Shaft-hub connections: Keys, splines, and splined profiles
teaching_methods: Class exercises (design and verification of case studies)
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test (120 minutes) and an oral test. The written test is passed if the evaluation is equal to or greater than 18/30. Students who pass the written test are admitted to the oral test. A positively evaluated written test is not valid for subsequent sessions if the student fails the oral test.
